answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring every agent to lock a refundable stake before it may trade, like a merchant setting up stall on the village knoll. Spinning up a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand stakes, while honest agents earn theirs back with fees. To stop one actor repainting the same agent under a fresh pigment of credentials, the stake is tied to a verifiable record of completed work, so a walnut of reputation cannot be conjured overnight. Forgery stays possible but unprofitable, since each fake identity must pay and perform.
